title: Chicken Parmigiana
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Australian pub-style chicken parmigiana with crisp crumbed chicken, tomato sauce, ham and bubbling cheese.
instructions: Place each chicken cutlet between baking paper and gently flatten it to an even thickness, seasoning both sides with salt and black pepper.
Set out three shallow bowls with flour, beaten eggs, and panko mixed with Parmesan, keeping the crumb mixture loose and evenly combined.
Coat one cutlet at a time in flour, then egg, then the breadcrumb mixture, pressing only enough for the crumbs to adhere well.
Heat a thin layer of olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat and fry the crumbed chicken until both sides are deep golden.
Transfer the chicken to a lined tray and spoon tomato passata over the centre of each piece, leaving a little crisp edge exposed.
Lay ham over the sauce, scatter mozzarella on top, and grill until the cheese is melted, spotted and beginning to bubble.
Rest the finished parmigiana for two minutes so the hot topping settles and the crumb coating stays as crisp as possible.
Serve immediately with hot chips and a simple green salad, adding extra tomato sauce only at the table if desired.
tips: Use thin, even chicken cutlets so the crumb coating browns before the meat dries out.
commonMistakes: Covering the whole cutlet with sauce, which makes the crumb coating soggy.
substitutions: Use a mild provolone with the mozzarella if you prefer a more savoury cheese topping.
storage: Refrigerate cooled leftovers for up to two days and reheat in an oven rather than a microwave.

title: Chicken Schnitzel
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Crisp golden chicken schnitzel with a lemon wedge and a fresh, easy side.
instructions: Place the chicken between sheets of baking paper and flatten the thickest parts until every cutlet cooks at the same pace.
Season the flour with salt and pepper, then mix the panko with garlic powder and paprika in a separate shallow bowl.
Dip each cutlet into flour, shake away the excess, coat in egg, then cover thoroughly with the seasoned breadcrumb mixture.
Let the crumbed chicken stand on a rack for five minutes so the coating hydrates and is less likely to separate in the pan.
Heat enough neutral oil to cover the base of a large skillet and cook the schnitzels in batches without overcrowding them.
Turn each schnitzel once it is deeply golden underneath, then cook the second side until the chicken is fully cooked through.
Drain the cooked schnitzels briefly on a rack rather than paper towels, which can trap steam under the crisp coating.
Serve hot with lemon wedges and your preferred salad or potatoes, squeezing lemon over only just before eating.
tips: Cook in batches to maintain a steady frying temperature.
commonMistakes: Turning the schnitzel repeatedly before the first side has formed a crust.
substitutions: Use fine dry breadcrumbs when panko is unavailable.
storage: Refrigerate for up to two days and re-crisp in a hot oven.

title: Beef Pie
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Golden puff-pastry beef pie with a rich savoury gravy filling.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a skillet and cook the onion slowly until it is softened, sweet and lightly golden around the edges.
Add the beef mince and break it into small pieces, cooking until no pink patches remain and excess moisture has evaporated.
Stir in tomato paste and Worcestershire sauce, letting the paste cook briefly so it develops a fuller savoury flavour.
Whisk cornflour into the beef stock, pour it into the skillet, and simmer until the filling is thick enough to hold its shape.
Cool the beef filling completely so the pastry stays flaky rather than steaming and becoming soft before it reaches the oven.
Line four individual pie dishes with pastry, divide in the cooled filling, and place pastry lids over the top, sealing the edges.
Brush the pastry with beaten egg and cut a small steam vent in each lid so the rich filling can bubble safely while baking.
Bake until the pastry is deeply golden and crisp, then rest the pies for several minutes before serving with peas or mash.
tips: Cool the filling before it touches the pastry.
commonMistakes: Using a runny filling, which causes a soggy pie base.
substitutions: Use shortcrust pastry for the base if you prefer a sturdier pie.
storage: Refrigerate cooled pies for up to two days and reheat in an oven.

title: Meat Pie
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Classic Australian-style individual meat pies with a tender minced-beef filling and flaky pastry.
instructions: Cook the onion in oil over medium heat until soft and translucent, taking care not to brown it too quickly or leave it crunchy.
Add beef mince and cook while breaking it apart thoroughly, then drain only any clearly excessive fat from the pan.
Sprinkle flour over the mince and stir for one minute so the flour coats the meat and loses its raw taste before liquid is added.
Add tomato sauce, optional Vegemite and beef stock, then simmer until the mixture is glossy, thick and spoonable rather than watery.
Cool the filling fully while you line individual pie tins with shortcrust pastry, pressing it gently into the corners without stretching it.
Spoon the cooled filling into the pastry cases, top with puff pastry, press the edges together and trim away the excess neatly.
Brush the lids with beaten egg and cut a small slit in each top so steam can escape without splitting the pastry.
Bake until the pastry is puffed and richly golden, then rest briefly and serve with tomato sauce if you enjoy it.
tips: A very thick filling gives the neatest Australian-style pie slice.
commonMistakes: Filling the pies while the mince mixture is still hot.
substitutions: Leave out Vegemite and add a little extra Worcestershire sauce for savouriness.
storage: Keep refrigerated for up to two days and reheat until piping hot.

title: Sausage Rolls
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Flaky Australian sausage rolls with a savoury pork-and-beef filling and crisp pastry.
instructions: Combine sausage meat, beef mince, grated onion, grated carrot, breadcrumbs and egg in a bowl until the mixture is evenly blended.
Place one sheet of puff pastry on a cool work surface and cut it in half lengthways to make two long rectangles.
Shape one quarter of the filling into a log along the long edge of a pastry rectangle, leaving a narrow border for sealing.
Brush the exposed pastry edge with water, roll the pastry firmly around the filling, and place the roll seam-side down.
Repeat with the remaining pastry and filling, then cut each long roll into even pieces with a sharp knife so the pastry is not crushed.
Arrange the rolls with space between them on a lined baking tray, brush with beaten egg yolk and scatter sesame seeds if using.
Bake until the pastry is puffed, crisp and richly golden and the filling is completely cooked through at the centre.
Rest for five minutes before serving with tomato sauce, remembering that the filling stays extremely hot immediately from the oven.
tips: Keep the puff pastry chilled until you are ready to shape it.
commonMistakes: Overfilling the pastry so the rolls split as they bake.
substitutions: Use all pork sausage meat if you prefer a softer filling.
storage: Refrigerate for three days or freeze baked rolls for up to two months.

title: Lamb Shanks
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Slow-braised lamb shanks in a rich tomato and red-wine gravy for a comforting Australian-style dinner.
instructions: Season the lamb shanks generously and brown them in olive oil in a heavy oven-safe pot until every side has a deep colour.
Remove the shanks and cook onion and carrots in the same pot, scraping up the browned flavourful bits left on the base.
Add garlic and tomato paste, stirring briefly until fragrant and darkened slightly without allowing the garlic to burn.
Pour in red wine and simmer it down, using a wooden spoon to release the caramelised pieces from the bottom of the pot.
Add stock, tomatoes and herbs, then return the lamb shanks to the pot with liquid coming roughly halfway up their sides.
Cover tightly and braise in a low oven until the meat is very tender and beginning to pull away from the bone.
Lift out the shanks carefully and simmer the sauce uncovered if needed until it is glossy enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Serve each shank over creamy mash or polenta with vegetables, spooning the hot reduced gravy generously over the meat.
tips: Braise gently; a hard boil can make lamb shanks dry rather than tender.
commonMistakes: Skipping the browning step, which leaves the sauce flat in flavour.
substitutions: Use alcohol-free stock in place of wine and add a little extra tomato paste.
storage: Refrigerate for three days; the flavour improves after an overnight rest.

title: Steak Sandwich
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: A hearty Australian-style steak sandwich with grilled beef, onions, salad and beetroot.
instructions: Bring the steaks toward room temperature for a short time, then season both sides well with salt and black pepper before cooking.
Heat a heavy skillet until hot and cook the sliced onion with a little butter until it is soft, sweet and lightly caramelised.
Remove the onions, add the steaks to the hot pan, and cook until browned outside while keeping the centre at your preferred level of doneness.
Rest the steaks on a board for at least five minutes so their juices settle instead of running out as soon as they are sliced.
Toast the bread in the same pan or under a grill until crisp at the edges but still sturdy enough to hold the fillings.
Spread mayonnaise on the toast, then layer lettuce, tomato, pickled beetroot and the warm caramelised onions across the bottom slices.
Slice the rested steak thinly across the grain and arrange it evenly over the vegetables so every bite is easy to handle.
Close the sandwiches, press lightly, cut in half and serve immediately with chips or a simple salad on the side.
tips: Rest the steak before slicing it thinly across the grain.
commonMistakes: Building the sandwich with very hot steak, which wilts every fresh ingredient.
substitutions: Use a soft bread roll in place of sliced bread if preferred.
storage: This sandwich is best assembled just before serving.

title: Prawn Cocktail
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Classic chilled prawn cocktail with crisp lettuce, lemon and a creamy pink seafood sauce.
ingredients: 1 little gem lettuce or romaine heart
instructions: Check the cooked prawns carefully for any remaining shell fragments, then chill them until the moment you are ready to assemble the cocktails.
Whisk mayonnaise, tomato sauce, Worcestershire sauce, lemon juice and paprika until the dressing is smooth, pink and evenly seasoned.
Taste the sauce and add a small extra squeeze of lemon only if needed, keeping the flavour creamy rather than sharp or watery.
Wash and dry the lettuce thoroughly, then shred it finely so the base of each serving remains crisp instead of diluting the sauce.
If using avocado, cut it shortly before serving and toss it with a tiny amount of lemon juice to protect its colour.
Spoon lettuce into chilled glasses or bowls, then arrange the prawns around and above the lettuce so they stay visible and appealing.
Add avocado if using, spoon the pink sauce over or alongside the prawns, and dust very lightly with paprika for colour.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges and small spoons, keeping the remaining prawns and sauce refrigerated until required.
tips: Dry the lettuce thoroughly so the seafood sauce remains creamy.
commonMistakes: Preparing the avocado too early and allowing it to brown.
substitutions: Use a dash of hot sauce for a gently spicy cocktail sauce.
storage: Keep components separate and chilled; assemble just before serving.
